source: Weyns and Calinescu 2015 [1] Table III (7-service TAS catalogue); Weyns and Iftikhar 2016 [13] Tables I and II (per-service Failure rate, Response time, Pending invocations); Camara et al. 2023 [10] (ms-canonical time scale, R2 = 26 ms anchor). Per-service mu derived by M/M/1 inversion per cstudies.md Table 7.3. Default TAS configuration {AS_3, MAS_4, DS_1} for the baseline per cstudies.md line 66 (DS_1 is the drug service in every scenario; AS_3 and MAS_3 are bottleneck candidates). Primary-source PDFs in assets/docs/CS/N1/. Operating-point ceiling at the E-QS canonical inflection (rho_b <= 0.65) derived in assets/notes/tgt/08/cs1/dasa-modelling.md Block 1 (lambda_z = 0.65 * 497 ~ 323 req/s).
notes: 13-artifact queueing network, baseline (no adaptation). TAS_1..TAS_6 are composite workflow stages (mu = 750 req/s, the 1.5x sensitivity floor per dasa-modelling.md Block 1); MAS_1..MAS_3 are the active Medical Analysis Services; AS_1..AS_3 are the active Alarm Services; DS_1 is the Drug Service (eps = 0.01). External arrivals enter at TAS_1 at lambda_z = 323 req/s; K = 16 uniform; c = 1 uniform. R1 = failure rate <= 1.0 % (Weyns 2015); R2 = response time <= 26 ms (Camara 2023). R3 retired 2026-05-13.

_labels.baseline: Baseline (no adaptation), loss-network with FAIL sink. Service nodes keep a self-loop = eps_i (error overload chi=(1+eps)lambda, load only, conserves flow). Failure is the handler leak to FAIL: TAS_4 leaks f_med, TAS_5 leaks f_alm, TAS_6 leaks eps_DS; survivors continue. availability = lambda_FAIL/lambda_z; self-loops do not change it.

environments._note: `_setpoint` names the default scenario for this config — the loader reads this scenario when no `--adaptation` CLI flag is given. `_routs[scenario][i][j]` = routing probability from node i to node j under `scenario`. Position i indexes into `_nodes[scenario]`. Diagonal captures per-service error probability; off-diagonal captures the TAS workflow routing.
